extracted.question: Did Medicare coverage for weight-management indications expand to beneficiaries with obesity absent other qualifying conditions?
extracted.answer: NOT via general statutory reinterpretation. Only via time-limited, voluntary demonstration/model authority (Medicare GLP-1 Bridge and BALANCE), and only subject to clinical criteria.
extracted.statutory_baseline: Since the inception of the Part D program, CMS has interpreted the statutory exclusion of 'agents when used for weight loss' to mean that a drug, when used for weight loss, is excluded from the definition of a covered Part D drug. This historical interpretation does not distinguish between use of a drug for treatment of individuals with obesity and individuals without obesity, so anti-obesity medications are only coverable in Part D if used to treat another condition with a medically accepted indication other than weight loss or weight management.
extracted.proposed_rule: CMS-4208-P (Contract Year 2026 Policy and Technical Changes), proposed November 2024, proposed to reinterpret the statutory exclusion so it would not apply to drugs when used to treat beneficiaries with obesity
extracted.proposed_rule_impact_estimate: would expand access to an additional 7 percent of the Part D population, or 3.4 million enrollees, with a cost of $24.8 billion to the Medicare program over a ten-year period
extracted.finalization_status: COULD NOT CONFIRM against a primary source that the reinterpretation was ever finalized. Domain-restricted search of cms.gov returned only the PROPOSED rule; no final-rule adoption of the reinterpretation was located. The absence of a finalized reinterpretation is consistent with CMS instead using demonstration authority (Bridge) and CMMI model authority (BALANCE).
extracted.operative_conclusion_for_tool: There is NO general, permanent Medicare Part D entitlement to GLP-1s for obesity alone. Access absent another qualifying indication runs through the Bridge (2026-07-01 to 2027-12-31, clinical criteria, PA required) or through a participating BALANCE Part D plan (CY2027 onward).

verbatim_excerpt: CMS proposes to reinterpret the statutory exclusion such that it would not apply to drugs when used to treat beneficiaries with obesity, which would expand access to an additional 7 percent of the Part D population, or 3.4 million enrollees, with a cost of $24.8 billion to the Medicare program over a ten-year period. -- NOTE: 'proposes' is the operative verb; reproduced from domain-restricted search output, not a direct read.
